classification.difficultyReason: Draw two given decompositions of a right trapezium. The only derived length is 15−11=4, and the triangle height 8 is shown.

content.prompt:
These two calculations show two ways to find the area of this shape.
Split the shape to represent these calculations.

answer.short: Draw a vertical line from the top edge down to the bottom-left corner.
answer.worked: Draw a vertical line from the top edge, $4\text{ cm}$ in from the left, down to the bottom-left corner. This gives an $11\text{ cm}$ by $8\text{ cm}$ rectangle and a triangle with base $15-11=4\text{ cm}$ and height $8\text{ cm}$: $88+16=104\text{ cm}^2$.

answer.short: Extend the bottom edge to the left and draw a vertical line down from the top-left corner to complete the enclosing rectangle.
answer.worked: Complete the enclosing $15\text{ cm}$ by $8\text{ cm}$ rectangle. The missing triangle has base $15-11=4\text{ cm}$ and height $8\text{ cm}$, so its area is subtracted: $120-16=104\text{ cm}^2$.
